findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
findings.body: The endpoint orders AuditLogEntry by '-datetime', but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key in paginator.py does math.floor/math.ceil directly on the attribute value and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. For a datetime field this raises TypeError when build_cursor computes keys (and compares a datetime column against an int in build_queryset), so the new optimized_pagination=true path returns 500 instead of audit logs for every authorized admin who enables it. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via timestamps; this paginator does not.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing of a Django queryset raises instead of paginating
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts any int), the code does queryset[negative:stop]. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it. A privileged user can therefore craft a cursor that 500s the audit-log endpoint, and the same unclamped is_prev offset at line 182/884 exposes BasePaginator users to the same crash.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: enable_advanced is computed as request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. For non-superuser requests where the organization context has no member (e.g. superuser-less API/token contexts that reach this endpoint, or members not yet resolved), evaluating .has_global_access on None raises AttributeError and 500s a previously working endpoint; the check is evaluated on every request, not only when optimized_pagination=true, because Python evaluates the right-hand side regardless of use_optimized's value only gated by the boolean expression order — actually enable_advanced is always computed before the if, so all non-superuser requests without a member regress.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction silently discards earliest-ending spans from segments
findings.body: Once a merged set exceeds a hardcoded 1000 members, zpopmin removes the lowest-scored members, where the score is now end_timestamp_precise. This silently deletes arbitrary child spans (those ending earliest) from a segment that will later be flushed as if complete, with no metric, log, or segment-too-large outcome as the previous flush-time check produced. It corrupts segment data rather than rejecting/skipping oversized segments, and the hardcoded 1000 also ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001) and any configured value.

findings.title: SET-to-ZSET conversion breaks in-flight Redis segments during deployment
findings.body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys in Redis are regular sets created by SADD. The new code unconditionally issues ZADD in process_spans, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN in add-buffer.lua, and ZSCAN in _load_segment_data against those same key names. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for these commands on set-typed keys, so during rollout every trace with an unflushed segment (up to redis_ttl=3600s old) errors in the consumer pipeline instead of being flushed; there is no key versioning, type check, or migration/drain step.

findings.title: Flush-time max_segment_spans guard removed with no equivalent for non-Lua growth
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer enforces max_segment_spans (the metric/log/skip branch was deleted). The only remaining cap is the Lua insert path, which does not cover segments already stored as sets, keys built by the initial batched ZADD before per-span Lua runs interleaved with other batches, or future writers. Oversized segments can now be loaded and produced downstream unbounded by span count, reintroducing the memory/downstream-size risk the guard existed for.

findings.title: Redirect chain traversal cut from 10000 to 1000 breaks deep segment trees
findings.body: The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects to find the canonical set for a span now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000, and the comment explaining that deeper trees may not join correctly was removed. Segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will resolve set_span_id to an intermediate span, so spans are split into multiple segments (flushed separately with wrong segment_id/is_segment attribution) — a silent correctness regression for deep traces that previously worked.

findings.title: Required end_timestamp_precise turns malformed/legacy spans into poison pills
findings.body: process_batch now does val['end_timestamp_precise'] with direct indexing for every message. Any span payload lacking that field (older producers, partial/relay variants the previous code tolerated since it never read the field) raises KeyError inside the batch function, failing the whole batch and causing redelivery of the same poison message indefinitely. The new Span field in buffer.py is also a required positional-or-keyword argument added before the defaulted is_segment_span, breaking any other Span(...) construction sites that don't pass it.
